### 1. Narrative, Pacing & Self-Explanatory Intro
- **Current state:** [slides.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/slides.html#L6-L85) starts with three text/code slides (`#paper`, `#big-ideas`, `#core-mechanisms`) before reaching the first interactive demo (`#interactive-demo`). Slide 1 assumes familiarity with grammars and nonterminals, and `#interactive-demo` doesn't state the interaction rules (*cut first, then fill; filled regions lock*). There is no takeaway slide after the demo.
- **What the feedback asks for:**
  - Open with a concise, jargon-free intro explaining *what a grammar/nonterminal is* and *why Markus Eger built Box-Split Grammars* (using a concrete example like splitting one wall into pillars and windows), or hook the reader right away with the interactive cutting demo and unpack the theory afterward.
  - Add clear on-slide instructions on the demo (cut first, then fill; filled regions lock) and a short takeaway slide right after it.

### 2. Python-Function Mechanics (`-1`, Constraints, Variants, Loops)
- **Current state:**
  - [demo/index.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/demo/index.html) ([codegen.js](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/demo/codegen.js)) and [demo/3d.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/demo/3d.html) ([codegen3d.js](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/demo/codegen3d.js)) only emit a single `@rule def structure():` with positive absolute sizes (`[size1, size2]`), `fill(...)`, and `void()`.
  - Nested rule calls (e.g., `wall()` calling `pillar()`/`window()`), `-1` proportional splits, `@rule(constraint=...)`, nondeterministic rule variants, and Python loops are not yet demonstrated interactively.
- **What the feedback asks for:**
  - **Negative / `-1` toggle:** Let users switch split sizes to proportional `-1` notation (and ideally resize the box to see `-1` flex while positive integers stay fixed).
  - **Constraints & random variants:** Show multiple `@rule` definitions sharing the same function name, arithmetic constraints on box dimensions, and a **Regenerate** button that re-samples valid variants.
  - **Loops & Python control flow:** Show how standard Python loops (e.g., repeating windows/floors) and function calls compose structures.

### 3. 3D Version & Possibilities Showcase
- **Current state:** [slides.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/slides.html#L102-L115) already embeds [demo/3d.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/demo/3d.html) (`#interactive-demo-3d`) for slicing and filling a 6×6×6 voxel box. There is no gallery/showcase slide of finished buildings or what the grammar can produce.
- **What the feedback asks for:**
  - Either expand the 3D experience into a recognizable Minecraft building preview (e.g., a house/temple/tower generated by rules) and/or add a dedicated **"Possibilities" slide** showing the range of structures Box-Split Grammars can generate.

### 4. Viewing Outside the Course Viewer & Formatting Issues
- **Why it looked like plain stacked text:** Per [CONTRIBUTING.md](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/CONTRIBUTING.md#L165-L180) and [decks.py](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/tools/decks.py#L14-L20), [slides.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/slides.html) is intentionally a **bare HTML fragment** (`<section class="slide">...`) meant to be wrapped by [serve.py](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/serve.py) or `build.py`. Opening `slides.html` directly in a browser loads no CSS or slide-deck JS, so every slide renders stacked vertically as plain text.
- **Formatting cleanups spotted in the files:**
  - [slides.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/slides.html#L91) and [slides.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/slides.html#L106) have leftover inline editor styles (`width: 1286.32px; max-width: none; ...`) on the demo subtitles.

Here is a concise summary of all the feedback received:

### 1. Structure, Pacing & Clarity
- **Hook sooner:** Move away from text-heavy upfront slides—get straight to the interactive cutting demo, then use slides afterward to explain how it works.
- **Make it self-explanatory:** Add an introduction defining basic terms (*grammar*, *nonterminal*) and explaining *why* Markus Eger created Box-Split Grammars (why box-splitting works well for buildings), grounded in a simple example like a wall split into pillars and windows.
- **Guide the demo:** Add clear instructions on the demo slide (*cut first, then fill; filled regions lock*) and a short takeaway slide immediately after.

### 2. Missing Paper Concepts in the Demos
- **Python-function side:** Readers understood nested box splitting, but not how the Python-function side of the grammar actually works.
- **Negative numbers / `-1` toggle:** Add a toggle to demonstrate `-1` proportional sizing alongside absolute block counts.
- **Constraints & random variants:** Show `@rule` constraints and nondeterministic variants in action—such as a **Regenerate** button that samples between different rule versions.
- **Loops:** Potentially demonstrate Python loops (`for` repetition) as well.

### 3. Visuals & Showcase
- **3D / Minecraft preview:** Include a 3D version or a 3D Minecraft-style preview.
- **Possibilities slide:** Add a slide showcasing the variety of buildings/structures Box-Split Grammars can generate.

### 4. Viewing & Formatting
- **Broken standalone viewing:** Outside the course viewer, the slides were hard to open and rendered as plain stacked text instead of a slideshow, with formatting issues.

Here are five concrete ways to elevate the visual polish of [slides.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/slides.html) and [style.css](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/style.css), building directly on the built-in primitives in [deck.css](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/engine/deck.css):

### 1. Replace Flat Colored Rectangles with Real Minecraft Voxel / Texture Art
- **Where:** Slide 2 (`#intro` wall diagram) and Slide 7 (`#possibilities` 4-card grid).
- **Why:** Right now those SVGs use flat solid fills (`#7c5b36`, `#b8945f`), which feel generic compared to the pixel-accurate Minecraft textures in [demo/textures.js](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/demo/textures.js) and the WebGL blocks in [demo/3d.html](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/box-split-grammars/demo/3d.html).
- **Example:** Render the Slide 2 wall and Slide 7 buildings using isometric SVG voxel cubes or tiled 16×16 SVG `<pattern>` block textures (Oak Log bark, Cobblestone, Oak Planks, Glass) so the slides look cohesive with the interactive demos.

### 2. Trade Heavy Card Borders & Shadows for Airy `deck.css` Highlighters
- **Where:** Slide 2 (`#intro`) and Slide 4 (`#takeaway-python`).
- **Why:** [deck.css](file:///c:/Users/USER/Desktop/Main/class/Sloth%20Lab/box-split-visual/explorables/engine/deck.css#L10-L16) is designed around open white space with colored markers rather than stacked bordered boxes. Right now Slide 2 has 3 tinted boxes next to a boxed SVG, and Slide 4 has 3 identical blue-bordered white cards.
- **Example:**
  - On Slide 2, drop the card borders/backgrounds on the left column and use clean typographic blocks with `<span class="hl">` yellow highlights (from `deck.css`) so the wall diagram becomes the clear visual focal point.
  - On Slide 4, rotate the 3 explanation items through the lab's palette (`--blue-tone`, `--sun-tone`, `--sea-tone` from `deck.css` lines 237–244) instead of repeating blue on all three.

### 3. Turn Demo Instructions into Scannable Step Pills
- **Where:** `.ch-head p` on Slides 3 (`#interactive-demo`), 5 (`#rules-demo`), and 6 (`#interactive-demo-3d`).
